keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. 'The kingdom bordered Aksu and Kashgar to the west and Karasahr and Turpan to the east'; 'The former area of Kucha now lies in present-day Aksu Prefecture, west-central Xinjiang'. A 150 km radius around Kuqa (60,000 km2) is the reading; the page gives no area. The infobox says 'Established: 2nd century BCE': the middle of the century is taken (confidence 1 in the ledger).

region.text: Kucha, between Aksu to the west and Karasahr to the east

ledger.note: 2nd century BCE: the kingdom of Qiuci appears. Infobox 'Established: 2nd century BCE'; 'In the second century BCE, the kingdom known in Chinese sources Qiuci was controlled' (by the Xiongnu). The page names no year; the middle of the century is the researcher's bridge. In 60 BCE 'the Han court established the Protectorate of the Western Regions'.

region.text: Kucha, between Aksu to the west and Karasahr to the east

ledger.note: 648: the Tang conquer Kucha. 'In 648, the Tang conquered Kucha, known to the Chinese as Qiuci, and made it the new seat of Anxi under the governance of Chai Zhewei from 649 to 651'; the Kucha page's infobox: 'Conquered by the Tang dynasty: 648 CE'. The Bai kings are listed to 'Bai Huan 731-789?' under Tang and Tibetan suzerainty, which the dossier does not draw as a state.

wars.outcome: The Tang took Kucha in 648 and made it the seat of the Anxi Protectorate in 649; Karasahr had fallen by 644.

certainty.note: An oasis kingdom: the page names neighbours (Aksu, Kashgar, Karasahr, Turpan) and no border.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks Kucha; ia-01-d asked for 'kingdom-of-kucha'). Thin: the page dates no early event and gives no area, no capital years and no king list beyond 'Suvarnadeva 625-645' and 'Bai Huan 731-789?'. The Tang dossier example already carries Kucha as a counterpart (the 648 conquest). The dossier ends in 648 (the infobox's Tang conquest) although the Bai dynasty reigned under Tang and Tibetan overlords to about 789; a gap-filler should add the Tibetan period (670-692, which the page does not give) if a state is wanted after 648. Kashgar (Shule), Karasahr (Yanqi) and Shanshan (Loulan) were not written: their pages were not opened. Gazetteer names used (Kuqa) resolve.
